title: Wi-Fi uses: station, access point, local services, and internet

spans.text: An ESP32 can use Wi-Fi to join a network or create its own network. These roles enable configuration, data collection, and local or internet-connected services.

STA (station) joins a router or phone hotspot and can reach the internet. AP (SoftAP) creates a network so a phone can open a configuration page. AP+STA runs both roles, sharing the radio and airtime. `WiFiScan` discovers nearby networks; `WiFiMulti` tries configured access points; `WebServer` serves a local HTTP page on the board. TCP/HTTP/WebSocket support browser control and two-way sessions; UDP suits small low-overhead messages; MQTT publishes events to a broker. mDNS helps find a device by name on a local network, NTP sets its clock, captive portals simplify first-time setup, and OTA delivers firmware. ESP-NOW sends short messages between compatible Espressif devices without a router; it is not internet access.

The three sketches below are alternatives, not one combined program. Internet access exists only if the STA's router has it.
WiFiMulti: connect to one of several configured access points

spans.title: Important safety and compatibility note
spans.text: Change the AP password, keep private network credentials out of the repository, and do not expose an unauthenticated HTTP control page to the internet. AP+STA, ESP-NOW, and concurrent-radio support vary by chip and core version.
